title: Topological charge switching in trapped polariton condensates
authors: Jaewon Kim, Hyun Gyu Song, Daegwang Choi, Yong-Hoon Cho
abstract: Topological charges in photonic systems provide a robust degree of freedom with direct applications in optical information processing. Bound states in the continuum (BICs) in photonic crystal slabs inherently carry such quantized topological charges, yet they are topologically protected, making active reconfiguration fundamentally challenging. Here, we demonstrate topological charge switching in trapped BIC polariton condensates in a photonic crystal, where spatial modulation of the photonic crystals supports multiple confined states, each carrying a distinct charge. Trapped condensates within the Dirac bandgap are expelled into the leaky band via polariton blueshift, enabling single-mode selection by solely tuning the excitation power. This work offers a platform for optically controlling topological charges by harnessing polariton nonlinearity.
summary: This paper demonstrates the active, all-optical switching of topological charges in polariton condensates confined within a photonic crystal. By tuning the excitation power, the system forces the condensate to switch between discrete, quantized topological states. This work establishes a novel platform for controlling topological properties using nonlinear optical interactions.
main_problem: The core challenge addressed is achieving active, all-optical reconfiguration (switching) of topological charges in photonic systems that are inherently topologically protected.
main_result: The authors successfully demonstrated topological charge switching in trapped polariton condensates by tuning the excitation power, causing the condensate to switch between distinct, quantized topological charge states.
method: The work combines experimental characterization using angle-resolved PL and reflectance spectroscopy with theoretical modeling using a 1D non-Hermitian Dirac Hamiltonian.
model_or_system: The system utilizes trapped exciton-polariton condensates within a photonic crystal well structure. The physics is modeled by a 1D non-Hermitian Dirac Hamiltonian, which describes the coupled dynamics of the polaritons.
key_observables: Topological charges ($q = +1$ to $+4$), quantized energy levels ($n=1, 2, 3, 4$), spectral blueshift, and single-mode occupancy.
important_parameters: Excitation power ($P$) relative to the condensation threshold ($P_{th}$), well lattice constant, and barrier bandgap energy.
main_assumptions: The switching mechanism is attributed to the polariton blueshift exceeding the barrier bandgap energy, and the system is modeled by the non-Hermitian Hamiltonian.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the schematic of the switching process, experimental confirmation of quantized states via PL spectra vs. well width, and the power-dependent transition showing the shift from one topological state to the next.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical platform (photonic crystal wells), confirms the existence of quantized trapped states, and then demonstrates the switching mechanism by showing how increasing excitation power drives the condensate into a higher-energy, different topological state.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, controllable platform for manipulating topological invariants using nonlinear optical effects (polariton nonlinearity), which is highly relevant for quantum information processing and open quantum systems research.
